Enterprise Systems Specialist

Grade: Grade 3

Job Purpose

The Enterprise Systems Specialist sits between first-line user support and second[1]and third-line vendor and infrastructure support. The role provides in-depth knowledge of the IPA's critical enterprise systems, coordinates system vendors and support partners, and acts as the IPA's internal subject matter expert for designated systems.

Reporting to the Head of ICT, the Specialist will strengthen issue resolution, improve

organisational ownership of enterprise applications, support vendor-managed

services and help deliver the IPA's Enterprise Systems Support Strategy. The role is

a specialist operational position rather than a senior management post.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Systems Support and Ownership

  • Administer, configure and support the IPA's portfolio of enterprise business applications, ensuring that systems remain reliable, secure and aligned with business requirements.
  • Act as the IPA's internal subject matter expert and knowledge custodian for designated enterprise systems.
  • Lead and maintain the structured handover of knowledge from external consultants and service providers, including configurations, integrations, customisations and significant historical decisions.
  • Investigate and resolve application, data and integration issues that are beyond first-line support but do not require vendor escalation.
  • Provide a single coordinating point for complex issues that cross application, infrastructure or supplier boundaries.
  • Maintain an informed view of application lifecycle requirements, technical debt, risks, dependencies and enhancement opportunities.

Cloud, Security, Data and Integrations

  • Manage and support cloud-based business applications and relevant Microsoft 365 services, working with vendors and support partners to maintain service performance and availability.
  • Support the administration and continuous improvement of enterprise security controls, including Identity and Access Management, role-based access, Multi-Factor Authentication and audit controls.
  • Monitor, maintain and troubleshoot system integrations, Application Programming

Interfaces, single sign-on services and data flows between enterprise platforms.

  • Support data quality, data governance and issue-resolution activities across enterprise systems and associated databases.
  • Support disaster recovery testing, system resilience planning, business continuity and cybersecurity activities relating to enterprise systems.

Vendor, Service and Change Management

  • Act as the primary operational liaison with software vendors, managed service providers and implementation partners for designated systems.
  • Validate proposed vendor solutions and coordinate the planning, testing and implementation of upgrades, enhancements, patches, releases and configuration changes.
  • Ensure that appropriate technical validation, user acceptance testing and business sign-off are completed before production deployment.
  • Scope change requests and out-of-scope work, helping the IPA to control cost, risk and supplier dependency.
  • Contribute to Service Level Agreement monitoring, supplier performance reviews, service reporting and continuous service improvement.
  • Maintain clear ownership of escalations and ensure that actions, decisions and outcomes are documented.

Projects, Reporting and Continuous Improvement

  • Participate in enterprise system implementations, migrations, upgrades and digital transformation initiatives, including requirements gathering, testing, user engagement and post-implementation support.
  • Develop and maintain operational reports, dashboards and management information to support service oversight and business decision-making.
  • Work with business stakeholders to identify opportunities for process improvement and better use of enterprise platforms.
  • Provide specialist advice to the Head of ICT on enterprise systems strategy, vendor capability, service risk and improvement priorities.
  • Maintain a practical roadmap of system improvements, lifecycle requirements and emerging risks.

Knowledge Management and Team Development

  • Develop and maintain system documentation, support procedures, knowledge articles, configuration records and operational standards.
  • Mentor and support ICT colleagues, strengthening internal technical capability and reducing dependency on individual resources or external suppliers.
  • Translate technical concepts into plain language for non-technical stakeholders and communicate business needs clearly to technical suppliers.
  • Undertake other appropriate duties consistent with the responsibilities and grade of the role.

About the ideal candidate

Qualifications

• A relevant third-level qualification in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional

experience (essential).

  • ITIL Foundation certification, or equivalent practical experience of IT service management (desirable).
  • Relevant Microsoft, cloud, cybersecurity, database or enterprise application certifications (desirable).

Knowledge

  • Cloud and Software as a Service delivery models.
  • Identity and Access Management, including role-based access, authentication and Multi-Factor Authentication.
  • Knowledge of principles including cybersecurity, security controls, data protection, governance requirements, service management, incident management, data structures and data quality principles
  • System integration concepts, Application Programming Interfaces and data exchange between enterprise platforms.
  • Reporting, data analysis or Business Intelligence tools.

Experience

  • Minimum five years’ relevant experience supporting, administering or managing enterprise business applications (essential).
  • Experience across the application lifecycle, including configuration, support, upgrades, enhancements and issue resolution. (essential).
  • Experience supporting cloud/SaaS enterprise applications, including Microsoft 365 or comparable environments (essential)
  • Experience contributing to system implementations, upgrades, migrations or digital transformation projects, including testing and transition to operational support (essential).
  • Experience managing vendors, service providers and third-party technology partners, including escalation of complex issues (essential).
  • Experience supporting system integrations, including APIs, Single Sign-On (SSO) and enterprise data flows(essential).
  • Experience producing and maintaining technical documentation, operational procedures and knowledge materials (essential).
  • Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Microsoft 365 administration or comparable enterprise platforms (desirable).
  • Experience with Learning Experience Platforms (LXPs) or other digital learning technologies (desirable).
  • Experience in education, public sector, professional services or another regulated environment (desirable).
  • Experience with business intelligence, reporting or data visualisation (desirable.)
  • Experience supporting business continuity, disaster recovery or system resilience (desirable).

Skills & Personal

Attributes

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex application, integration and data issues.
  • Strong stakeholder-management and communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences
  • Ability to work effectively with external suppliers’ while maintaining appropriate organisational ownership and oversight.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise competing operational, project and support demands.
  • A structured and disciplined approach to documentation, knowledge management and operational procedures.
  • Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
  • Collaborative approach with a strong customer service focus, and commitment to teamwork.
  • A commitment to continuous improvement and identifying opportunities to improve the effectiveness, resilience and use of enterprise systems.

Health

• Each candidate shall be in a state of health such as would

indicate a reasonable prospect of ability to render regular

and effective service

Conscia will be managing all aspects of the recruitment process on behalf of The Institute of Public Administration. Applications should be made online through Recruitment Services | Conscia Talent and by attaching a completed application form, downloadable at the link above.

Your application must be submitted on the Recruitment Services | Conscia Talent website no later than 1pm (Irish time) on Monday 14th December 2026.

If you do not receive an acknowledgement of receipt of your application within 24 hours of applying, please email: ipa@consciatalent.com

Governance Specialist (Assurance)

Grade: Grade 3

Professional Development in the IPA:

The IPA Professional Development department delivers non-accredited and

professionally accredited programmes that advance the understanding, standard and

practice for public servants in key skill areas.

Job Function: The Governance Specialist will lead on and contribute to the

delivery, development, administration, promotion and evaluation of the Institute’s

Governance services and programmes to clients of the IPA. This role entails

providing capability-building training and advisory services to clients such as

Government Departments, State Bodies, Local Authorities and Higher Education

Institutions, and at all levels, including Boards, Committees, Senior Teams, Officials

and staff. The role-holder will work as part of an integrated and collaborative team

within the Professional Development Department in the IPA.

The successful candidate will be an experienced professional with strong

communication skills and track record which will further strengthen the Governance

Team and deliver high-quality services to clients.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities

Professional Development and Advisory

  • Design, organise and deliver professional development programmes for boards, committees, senior leaders and staff across areas including governance, risk, audit, assurance, strategy, compliance, cyber/data governance, legal obligations and finance.
  • Deliver training through both in-person and online formats, tailoring content to

client requirements where appropriate.

  • Collaborate with Governance Team colleagues and wider IPA staff in the development and delivery of programmes, including co-facilitation where required.
  • Respond promptly to client training requests and requests for quotation (RfQs).
  • Maintain and enhance training materials to reflect emerging developments, trends and best practice.
  • Support the development of Governance Forum events, including topic selection, speaker engagement and event moderation.
  • Maintain accurate training records and pipeline information, ensuring high levels of client satisfaction, timely invoicing and achievement of budget

targets.

Advisory

  • Lead and contribute to the development of proposals and responses to client requests for advisory services across governance, risk, audit, assurance, strategy, compliance, cyber/data governance, legal obligations and finance.
  • Lead or support advisory assignments, working collaboratively to deliver high-quality client outcomes.
  • Ensure effective project planning, management and delivery, producing high-quality reports and outputs that meet client expectations.

Business Development

  • Lead the preparation of proposals and RfQ responses, ensuring solutions are aligned with client requirements.
  • Identify and pursue new business opportunities in line with team priorities, emerging governance needs and IPA Strategy, Learning for Tomorrow, Empowering Ireland’s Future Ready Public Service (2026-2030)
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, Governance Forum members, key stakeholders, colleagues and associates to understand requirements and identify emerging opportunities.
  • Monitor developments, research and best practice in public sector and corporate governance to inform service development, events, programme content and IPA thought leadership.

General

  • Engage in continuous professional development to maintain and enhance professional expertise, training capability and sector knowledge.
  • Work collaboratively with administrative and corporate support teams to ensure effective service delivery.
  • Support budget planning, performance monitoring, service development and process improvement initiatives within the team.
  • Undertake additional duties as required and contribute to the wider work and development of the Governance Team wider IPA.

About the ideal candidate

Qualifications

  • A third level qualification in Corporate Governance or a related field (e.g. Finance, Public Administration, Social Science) (Essential)
  • A post-graduate qualification in a relevant area above (Desirable)
  • An accounting / auditing qualification with relevant practitioner experience ideally in a public service body or publicly funded body (Desirable)
  • Qualification in training and development or a related area (Desirable)

Knowledge

  • Strong, demonstrable knowledge of corporate governance, including requirements, expectations and challenges for boards and organisations
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of the public service and public service accountability environment
  • Familiarity and understanding of professional development trends and needs in the public service

Experience

  • Minimum 4 years’ professional experience at an appropriate level working in a governance role or governance adjacent role (e.g. finance, audit, risk, compliance/legal, cyber/data governance, corporate services) (Essential)
  • At least 2-3 years’ experience working as an auditor or accountant (Desirable)
  • At least 2-3 years’ experience working in a public service body or publicly funded body (Essential)
  • At least 1-2 years’ experience in lecturing or training (Desirable)
  • Experience in cyber/data/AI governance (Desirable)
  • Demonstrable experience in managing a wide and diverse workload and competing demands and deadlines
  • Demonstrable experience in presentation and paper/report writing to a high standard

Skills

  • Excellent communication skills, including presentation and group facilitation
  • Excellent client relationship management skills
  • Strong organisational and planning abilities
  • Strong research, analytical and writing skills
  • Ability to analyse data and participant feedback to improve training effectiveness
  • Creative problem-solving skills and adaptability
  • Strong in MS Office including word, PowerPoint, excel and other software packages (e.g. audience engagement, survey)

Personal attributes

  • Comfortable working with senior executives, officials and board and committee members
  • High level of integrity and professionalism
  • Attention to detail and quality of work outputs
  • Self-motivated and ability to work effectively alone (leading assignments) as well as within a Team and with wider IPA colleagues
  • Ability to work under pressure and to deliver to tight deadlines, within the context of competing demands
  • Passionate about public service, governance and capability development
  • Approachable, with the ability to build rapport with a diverse range of participants and clients
  • Adaptable to diverse groups and learning environments
  • Willingness to travel within Ireland for training delivery
  • Fluent in English, with proficiency in Irish being an advantage

Health

• Each candidate shall be in a state of health such as would indicate a reasonable prospect of ability to render regular and effective service

Conscia will be managing all aspects of the recruitment process on behalf of The Institute of Public Administration. Applications should be made online through Recruitment Services | Conscia Talent and by attaching a completed application form, downloadable at the link above.

Your application must be submitted on the Recruitment Services | Conscia Talent website no later than 1pm (Irish time) on Friday 11th December 2026.

Specialist in Strategic Human Resource Management and People Development

Grade: Grade 3

Professional Development in the IPA:

The IPA Professional Development department delivers non-accredited and

professionally accredited programmes that advance the understanding, standard and

practice for public servants in key skill areas.

Role Overview:

The Specialist will be part of the Strategic Human Resource Management and

People Development Team, which designs and delivers professional development

programmes for civil and public service organisations.

The primary focus of the role is to develop the knowledge, skills and capability of

managers and HR professionals across the public sector through the design,

delivery and evaluation of high-quality learning interventions. The Specialist will act

as a subject matter expert, translating HRM, employee relations and employment

law principles into practical learning experiences that support effective people

management in client organisations.

The Specialist will ensure that all learning content reflects current employment

legislation, public sector HR and industrial relations practice, and the CIPD

Profession Map. The role will also contribute to programmes that support learners in

progressing towards CIPD accreditation and professional membership, helping

participants translate learning into recognised professional development and

practice.

Principal Duties

Programme Design & Delivery

• Design, develop and deliver learning programmes across the employee lifecycle, with particular emphasis on:

o Probation and performance management

o Employee engagement and development

o Managing underperformance

o Challenging conversations and conflict resolution

o Disciplinary, grievance and dignity at work procedures

o Mediation, workplace investigations and terminations

o Equality, working time, protected disclosures and procedural fairness

• Ensure programmes reflect:

o The CIPD Profession Map and associated standards

o Current employment legislation and codes of practice

o Public sector HR and industrial relations best practice

o Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) and Labour Court procedures

o The Civil and Public Service Capability Framework

• Deliver learning that develops understanding of:

o WRC and Labour Court processes

o Mediation, conciliation, adjudication and dispute resolution

o Case preparation, documentation and claims management

o Public sector obligations and relevant precedents

CIPD and Professional Accreditation

  • Contribute to the design and delivery of programmes that support progression towards CIPD accreditation and membership.
  • Act as a subject matter expert in maintaining alignment between IPA programmes and CIPD standards.
  • Support learners throughout the journey from programme participation to professional recognition, including:

o Advising on eligibility for CIPD Associate Membership

o Supporting membership application processes where appropriate

o Liaising with CIPD to maintain alignment with accreditation and

o membership requirements

• Ensure assessment, learner records and programme outcomes are appropriately documented to support accreditation, quality assurance and reporting requirements.

Client Engagement and Relationship Management

  • Engage with clients to identify learning, development and consultancy requirements.
  • Provide expert guidance to clients on complex HRM and IR challenges.
  • Collaborate with colleagues on programme development, delivery and continuous improvement to achieve positive outcomes for clients and learners.

Other general duties

  • Organise appropriate conferences, seminars, workshops and events.
  • Contribute to programme administration, business cycle planning, promotion and business development activities as required.
  • Undertake such other duties as may be assigned from time to time.

About the ideal candidate

Qualifications

• A third level qualification (minimum NFQ Level 8) in Human Resources, Employment Law, Business, or a closely related field (essential).

  • CIPD Associate, Chartered Member (MCIPD) or Chartered Fellow (FCIPD), or working towards same (essential).
  • Postgraduate qualification in HRM, Employment Law, Adult Education or a related field (desirable).
  • Professional qualification in training and development (minimum QQI Level 6) (desirable).
  • Qualification in mediation, conflict resolution, coaching or organisation development (desirable).

Knowledge

  • Strong knowledge of HRM, employee relations and Irish employment legislation (essential).
  • Knowledge of Irish public sector HR and industrial relations frameworks (essential).
  • Knowledge of WRC and Labour Court procedures and relevant codes of practice (essential).
  • Knowledge of the CIPD Profession Map and professional standards and membership pathways.
  • Understanding of the Civil Service Capability Framework and its application in learning design.
  • Understanding of the Public Sector Equality and Human Rights duty.

Experience

  • Minimum 4 years’ professional experience at an appropriate level working in role(s) centred on HR management, training, or organisational development (essential).
  • Demonstrated experience delivering training across multiple stages of the employee lifecycle (essential).
  • At least 2-3 years’ experience in lecturing or training (desirable).
  • Experience of designing and/or delivering learning aligned to CIPD standards
  • Experience in curriculum design and programme development.
  • Experience working within or with public-sector agencies.
  • Demonstrable experience in managing a wide and diverse workload and competing demands and deadlines
  • Demonstrable experience in presentation and paper/report writing to a high standard

Skills

  • Excellent training and facilitation skills including presentation and communication skills.
  • Ability to explain complex employment-law and IR concepts in accessible, practical terms.
  • Strong client-relationship management skills.
  • Ability to analyse data and participant feedback to improve training effectiveness.
  • Ability to manage group dynamics and facilitate challenging conversations.
  • Strong research, analytical and writing skills.
  • Proficiency in virtual delivery technologies (Zoom, MS Teams, Webex).
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office and digital learning tools.

Personal attributes

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team.
  • Commitment to Institute-wide development and self-development.
  • Demonstrate flexibility in adapting to changing requirements.
  • Commitment to quality delivery, continuous improvement and client focus.
  • Fluent in English, with proficiency in Irish being an advantage
  • Approachable, with the ability to build rapport with a diverse range of participants and clients
  • Adaptable to diverse groups and learning environments
  • Willingness to travel within Ireland for training delivery

Key Details:

Location: Dublin

Contract: Full-time, Specified Purpose Contract*

*The specified purpose is a Backfill (Approximate until October/2027)

Salary: €43,071 - €64,166 *

*The successful candidate will be placed on the first point of the salary scale unless they have existing public sector experience

Closing date: Monday, 30 November 2026 at 3pm

Application Form: Failte Ireland_Support, Business, Festivals and Major Sports Events (Temporary, SPC, Full-time) _Application Form.docx

To support the development and conversion of international business event opportunities that deliver economic, social and environmental benefits for Ireland. The role works collaboratively with conference ambassadors, industry partners and international stakeholders to help secure high-value international conferences and strengthen Ireland's position as a leading business events destination.

Job Purpose:

Primary Objectives/Key Responsibilities

  • Support the identification, development and conversion of international conference opportunities for Ireland.
  • Assist conference ambassadors and industry partners in securing high-value business events.
  • Conduct market research, lead generation and pipeline management activities.
  • Support the delivery of sales, marketing and bid development initiatives.
  • Build and maintain positive relationships with stakeholders, clients and industry partners.
  • Assist with events, communications and promotional activities.
  • Maintain accurate records and reporting using CRM and other business systems.
  • Ensure compliance with organisational policies, procedures and sustainability objectives.
  • Contribute to team projects and support the achievement of Business Events programme targets.

Carry out all other duties as required from time to time.

Person Specification:

  • Strong presentation and communication skills.
  • Excellent organisational and administrative skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines effectively.

Essential Criteria:

In order to be eligible to apply for this role you must have / demonstrate in your application form the following:

  • A minimum of 2 years' experience in a relevant role. in Business, Tourism, Marketing, Communications, Event Management or a related area
  • A professional qualification (minimum Level 6 under the QQI Framework) in Business, Tourism, Marketing, Communications, Event Management or a related discipline.
  • High level of proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Experience using CRM systems and maintaining accurate records.
  • Experience of working with a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders to achieve business objectives.
  • Experience in researching, coordinating or supporting projects, programmes or business development activities.
  • Experience in preparing and delivering presentations and written communications to a professional standard.

Desirable Requirements:

  • Experience working within the tourism, events, hospitality or business events sector.
  • Knowledge of the business events and/or leisure tourism sectors.
  • Experience supporting sales, business development or marketing initiatives.
  • Demonstrable ability to work collaboratively as part of a team.
  • Demonstrate a knowledge of sustainability and responsible tourism principles.

Key Competencies

  • Managing Relationships
  • Communicating Effectively
  • Commercial Awareness
  • Planning and Managing Work

Office Location and Blended Working:

We do not ask for addresses as part of the application process, however it is the responsibility of the candidate to acknowledge the base location of the role. The successful candidate must regularly work from and attend the base office location of the role.

Please note: Remote working from outside the State is not permitted other than in exceptional circumstances. As this role is within the Irish public service, the post-holder must carry out a minimum of 80% of their working time within the State (Republic of Ireland). Candidates who reside in Northern Ireland must be able to meet this requirement.

  • This role requires travel, with attendance at a number of national and regional locations / sites on an annual basis.
  • The flexibility to travel domestically, and on occasion internationally is an element of this role
  • This role will require working unsocial hours including bank holidays

Selection Process:

Shortlisting will be based on applications and the selection process may involve two competency based interviews. A panel of successful candidates may be formed following the selection process.

Interview Attendance Requirement:

Candidates must be available to attend an in-person interview at the location and date specified by Fáilte Ireland. Please note that the location of the interview may vary from the base location of the role.

Interview Dates

Please ensure that you are available to attend both interview stages on the dates outlined below, should you be successful in progressing through the recruitment process.

  • First-Round Interview (R1): 6th January 2027
  • Second-Round Interview (R2): 14th January 2027

Please note that these dates are fixed and cannot be changed. Candidates should take this into consideration before submitting their application.

Salary and Benefits

€43,071 - €64,166 *

*This role will be filled in line with Public Pay Policy at Point 1 of the relevant Salary Scale unless the successful candidate is appointed from an existing public sector role.

The Annual Leave allowance for this post is 23 days.

Further details on the benefits on offer can be found in the Why Work with Fáilte Ireland? | Fáilte Ireland · Failte Ireland

How to Apply

Conscia will be managing all aspects of the recruitment process on behalf of Fáilte Ireland

On this page, you can click on and download the Application form below:

job.title: Support, Consumer Marketing (Temporary, Full-time)
job.description:
Key Details:

Location: Dublin

Contract: Full-time, Temporary, Specific Purpose Contract *

*The specific purpose is to cover a Maternity Leave (Approx duration 13 months)

Salary: €43071 - €64166 (starting at the first point of the scale)

Closing date: Thursday, 26 November 2026 at 3pm

Application Form: Failte Ireland_Support, Consumer Marketing (Temporary, Full-time) _Application Form.docx

Job Purpose:

The successful candidate will provide administrative and marketing support to the Consumer Marketing Team to maximise the development and delivery of world class marketing communications that will encourage Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland consumers to take increased short breaks in the Republic of Ireland. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to play a pivotal role in the delivery of award-winning marketing campaigns and work with best-in-class agency partners.

The successful candidate will also be part of the team Responsible for marketing Ireland’s tourism experiences, highlighting festivals, food, sport, culture, and other unique experiences that drive visitor interest and travel.

Note: Our partner agency, Tourism Ireland, has the responsibility of marketing the Island of Ireland to overseas holidaymakers. We work very closely in partnership with them as they develop global campaigns.

At Failte Ireland we are brand builders. The successful candidate will play a key role in developing and building our brands Wild Atlantic Way (WAW), Ireland’s Ancient East (IAE), Ireland’s Hidden Heartlands (IHH) and Dublin.

Primary Objectives/Key Responsibilities

  • Support the development and implementation of an effective brand(s) communication strategy and implementation programme, utilising all channels to build awareness, increase intention and ultimately deliver increased volume and revenue from all target visitor segments in ROI & NI.
  • Support the development of content and campaigns that highlight the experiences that motivate travel to Ireland, including major events, festivals, sport, food and drink, culture, heritage and outdoor activities.
  • Assist with project management for the delivery of marketing campaigns and projects, including taking individual responsibility for managing specific elements of campaigns, working both with the wider team and also under own initiative.
  • Supporting the guardianship of our brands and creative assets by working with internal teams and agency partners on usages, asset storage and adherence to brand guidelines.
  • Assist the team in working closely with key agency partners.
  • Support the team in reporting on data, learnings and ROI analysis from marketing campaigns.
  • Support the coordination and preparation of content/presentations for brands, partners and/or internal meetings as required.
  • Support the development of campaign content, consumer messaging and marketing assets across paid, owned and earned channels.
  • Support the coordination of activities for shoots, media and other partners.
  • Work closely with the wider marketing and digital team to drive efficiencies and maximise content distribution and impact.
  • Collaborate with other internal teams to deliver an effective marketing work programme.
  • To support the wider organisation with their communications in terms of recommending and advising on the best channels to deliver to maximise our reach.
  • Responsible for administration and financial management tasks in line with Fáilte Ireland policy.
  • Provide logistics support for meetings/workshops/events by setting up venue, organising room layout, booking accommodation, dealing with invitees.
  • Record, produce and distribute minutes of meetings.
  • Carry out all other duties as required and participate as a full member of the Marketing Team by supporting different work projects, as required, from time to time.

The flexibility to travel domestically, internationally, and work unsociable hours may be required.

Person Specification

  • Applicants must meet the essential criteria and demonstrate, through relevant examples in their application, the key competencies outlined below.

Essential Criteria:

In order to be eligible to apply for this role you must have / demonstrate in your application form the following:

  • A minimum of two years' experience in consumer marketing, marketing communications or campaign management, gained either in-house or within an agency environment.
  • One year experience in a marketing communications role at a large consumer brand driven organisation (or a comparable role within a marketing agency or similar company).
  • Experience working with within an agency or with agency partners
  • Microsoft Office Proficiency.
  • Strong organisational skills with administrative and budget processing experience
  • Experience collaborating and working cross functionally with other teams and stakeholders.
  • A professional qualification (minimum Level 6 under the QQI Framework) in Marketing, Communications, Business, Digital Marketing or a related discipline. is essential

Desirable Requirements:

  • Knowledge of Fáilte Ireland brands and the broader Irish tourism product offering
  • A Professional Qualification (Level 8 under the QQI Framework) in a related discipline
  • Experience in supporting integrated marketing campaigns ie. including ATL (TV, radio, OOH) as well as BTL digital and social media elements.
  • Experience with marketing technology e.g. tools for managing workflows and/ or analytics tools to gain customer insights.

Key Competencies

  • Team Work
  • Planning and Managing Work
  • Communicating Effectively
  • Managing Relationships

Office Location and Blended Working:

We do not ask for addresses as part of the application process, however it is the responsibility of the candidate to acknowledge the base location of the role. The successful candidate must regularly work from and attend the base office location of the role.

Please note: Remote working from outside the State is not permitted other than in exceptional circumstances. As this role is within the Irish public service, the post-holder must carry out a minimum of 80% of their working time within the State (Republic of Ireland). Candidates who reside in Northern Ireland must be able to meet this requirement.

Selection Process:

Shortlisting will be based on applications and the selection process may involve two competency based interviews. A panel of successful candidates may be formed following the selection process.

Interview Attendance Requirement:

Candidates must be available to attend an in-person interview at the location and date specified by Fáilte Ireland. Please note that the location of the interview may vary from the base location of the role.

Interview Dates

Please ensure that you are available to attend both interview stages on the dates outlined below, should you be successful in progressing through the recruitment process.

  • First-Round Interview (R1): 15th December 2026
  • Second-Round Interview (R2): 21st December 2026

Please note that these dates are fixed and cannot be changed. Candidates should take this into consideration before submitting their application.

Salary and Benefits

€43,071 – €64,166*.

*This role will be filled in line with Public Pay Policy at Point 1 of the relevant Salary Scale unless the successful candidate is appointed from an existing public sector role.

The Annual Leave allowance for this post is 23 days.

Further details on the benefits on offer can be found in the Why Work with Fáilte Ireland? | Fáilte Ireland · Failte Ireland

Conscia will be managing all aspects of the recruitment process on behalf of Fáilte Ireland

Late applications will be ineligible for consideration. Therefore, it is your responsibility to ensure that you have allowed sufficient time for transmission of your application.

job.title: Electrification Support Engineer
job.description:
Electrification Support Engineer

An exciting opportunity to play a key role in supporting Dublin Bus’s transition to an electric fleet.

We’re looking for an experienced EV/EV Charging Engineer to ensure the charging infrastructure, chargers, vehicles and Charge Management System are operating reliably and efficiently across Dublin Bus depots.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Monitor and troubleshoot EV charging systems and infrastructure
  • Act as the technical point of contact for suppliers, contractors and service providers
  • Manage incidents, root-cause analysis and technical changes through to resolution
  • Support depot teams with technical guidance and training
  • Help develop processes and support future phases of fleet electrification

What we’re looking for:

  • Engineering qualification or relevant technical/trade background
  • Strong experience with EV charging / electrification
  • Knowledge of OCPP, ISO 15118 and/or VDV protocols
  • Experience in technical support, service delivery or operational engineering
  • Experience managing vendors, SLAs and incident resolution
  • A genuine interest in EV technology and fleet electrification

Location: Dublin

This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to be directly involved in keeping a growing electric bus fleet operational and supporting the next stage of Dublin’s transport electrification.

job.title: Electrical Engineer
job.description:
About IN2

Formed in 2002, IN2 is a progressive engineering consultancy operating across Ireland, the UK, and Europe, dedicated to creating better spaces for people. With over 100 experts across six locations, our team of engineers, technicians, and consultants collaborate closely with clients and partners to deliver innovative, sustainable, and energy-efficient building solutions across a wide range of sectors—from concept and design through to handover and beyond.

For over 20 years, we have maintained a people-centric culture that encourages growth, innovation, and adaptability. Our award-winning MEP projects, combined with recognition as a ‘Great Place to Work’, reflect our commitment to quality, sustainability, and a supportive, inclusive work environment where individuals can thrive.

At IN2, joining our team means being part of a collaborative, high-performing, and forward-thinking organisation, where your contribution makes a real impact—and where career opportunities grow alongside our business.

Working Hours

We operate a 37.5-hour working week designed to support work-life balance. We offer flexible start and finish times between 8am and 6pm, provided that core hours of 10am to 4pm are covered for team collaboration and meetings.

About The Role

We are seeking an experienced Electrical Engineer to join our growing Athlone team. This is a permanent position offering an excellent package for the right candidate. You’ll play a key role in project delivery and receive mentorship from senior engineers to support your career development.

What you will do

Athlone offers the chance to do career-defining work without long commutes or city pressure. You will be trusted, supported, and encouraged to shape how things are done locally, with full backing from the wider IN2 team. As a Senior Electrical Engineer at our Athlone Office, you will:

  • Assist senior engineers with project management, on-site inspections, technical surveys, and design team meetings
  • Play an active role in project delivery from concept through to completion
  • Support the management team in client relationships, budgeting, and reporting
  • Contribute to mentoring junior staff, reviewing design work, and providing guidance
  • Collaborate with senior engineers for ongoing mentorship and growth

Your Experience

To be considered for this role, you should have:

Essential

  • Degree in Building Services Engineering or Electrical Engineering
  • Minimum of 4 years’ experience in electrical design, ideally within a consultancy environment
  • Passion for career progression and aspiration to achieve Chartered status (if not already obtained)

Why You’ll Love Being Part of the Team

At IN2, we’ve traded the stuffy corporate ladder for a flat hierarchy and a culture where your voice actually matters. We’re a diverse, collaborative team that believes the best ideas can come from anyone, anywhere.

  • Global Impact, Local Feel: You’ll get to work on game-changing projects across different countries, supported by our specialist BIM, Sustainability, and Building Physics teams.
  • Constant Growth: Through IN2 Talks, cross-office collaboration, and a culture of knowledge sharing, you’re always learning something new.
  • Your Best Self: We prioritise a genuine work-life balance with flexible hours and support for personal circumstances. We’re big on open communication and ensuring our workplace is a bias-free zone where you can truly be yourself.

What’s In It For You?

We’ve put together a package that looks after your wallet, your career, and your wellbeing.

The Essentials

  • Competitive Pay & Bonuses: A salary that reflects your worth, plus an annual bonus and pension contributions.
  • Annual Leave: 22 days of annual leave, scaling up to 27 days as you grow with us (plus all those bank holidays!).
  • Flexible Hours: Work-life balance isn't just a buzzword here—we offer a 37.5-hour working week with flexible hours (8am–6pm), to suit your lifestyle!

Career Progression

  • Personal Roadmap: You’ll have a dedicated Personal Development Plan and mentoring from our senior leaders.
  • The IN2 Academy: Access to our internal academy, CPD support, and expert assistance in advancing your career,

Health & Wellbeing

  • Mind & Body: Access to our Employee Assistance Program, annual health checks, and various fitness initiatives.
  • Commute Greener: Take advantage of our Cycle to Work scheme to keep active on your way to the office.

Social & Community

  • Legendary Events: From our famous Christmas party weekend to Employee Appreciation Day and regular staff social events.
  • Giving Back: Get involved with our team-led charity initiatives.
  • International Reach: opportunities to work across IN2 offices in London, Dublin, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone, and Madrid

Eligibility: Due to regulatory requirements, this role is open to candidates with permanent residency or unrestricted right to work in Ireland only. Applications requiring visa sponsorship cannot be considered.

job.title: Senior Electrical Engineer
job.description:
Senior Electrical Engineer

Own the outcome. Not just the design.

Senior Engineers at IN2 lead from the front, responsible for decisions, direction, and delivery across multiple high-value projects.

The Role

As a Senior Electrical Engineer at IN2, you will take ownership of electrical design delivery across major projects, helping shape technical

direction, maintain quality, and build trusted relationships with clients and project teams. This is a hands-on role for someone who can

lead confidently, think strategically, and deliver to a high standard.

What You'll Do

  • Lead electrical design across multiple high-value projects
  • Oversee technical delivery and quality standards
  • Act as a key client contact and build long-term relationships
  • Coordinate with internal teams and external stakeholders
  • Mentor and support junior engineers
  • Contribute to innovation and sustainability strategies

What You'll Bring

  • Degree in Electrical or Building Services Engineering
  • 6+ years' experience in electrical design
  • Strong technical knowledge of building systems and standards
  • Experience leading projects and managing clients
  • Chartered or working towards Chartership desirable
  • Strong leadership and communication skills

What You'll Get

This isn't built around perks. It's built around how high-performing engineers actually want to work. Real ownership, real progression,

and a culture that trusts you to deliver.

The Essentials

  • Competitive salary, bonus and pension that reflect your impact
  • 22 to 27 days annual leave, plus bank holidays
  • Flexible working across a 37.5 hour week: early start or later start? you decide

Career Progression

  • A clear path forward, with responsibility increasing as you prove it
  • Direct exposure to senior leaders, not layers of hierarchy
  • IN2 Academy, CPD support and chartership guidance
  • Fully paid professional fees

Health and Wellbeing

  • Employee Assistance Programme and annual health checks
  • Wellbeing and fitness initiatives that support you long term
  • Cycle to Work scheme to make the everyday easier

Social and Community

  • Genuinely strong team culture, built through regular events and shared wins
  • Employee-led charity initiatives with real involvement
  • Offices in Dublin, London, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone and Madrid

Why IN2?

Across every role, electrical, mechanical, or BIM, the IN2 difference is the same: you're expected to think, lead, and shape outcomes, not just execute instructions. Here's what sets us apart.

Ownership from Day One

Whether you're an Engineer or a Senior, you'll have real accountability and decision-making authority. No waiting for permission. No layers of sign-off slowing you down.

Progression Based on Ability

Faster progression based on what you deliver, not how long you've been in the seat. A clear pathway from Engineer to Senior, Associate, and beyond.

Innovation Time

Dedicated time to develop new ideas, explore emerging technologies, and contribute to sustainability strategies: built into how we work, not bolted on.

High-Performance, Low-Ego Culture

A team that challenges each other, supports each other, and wins together. No hierarchy for hierarchy's sake. Just talented people doing exceptional work.

Complex, High-Profile Projects

Exposure to design-led, high-impact developments that push the boundaries of what building services engineering can achieve.

Global Reach

Work across offices in Dublin, London, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone, and Madrid- a genuinely international practice with a collaborative, connected culture.

Ready to own the outcome? Join a team that expects more and gives more in return.

job.title: Cyber Underwriter
job.description:
Does it ever feel like you’re underwriting with one hand tied behind your back? Tired of the struggles and inefficiencies associated with legacy systems and processes? Spending too much of your time and energy navigating corporate politics? All leaving your efforts to innovate and deliver underwriting excellence languishing?

At Ledgebrook, we believe a career in underwriting can be so much more. You bring the passion and entrepreneurial spirit; we’ll provide the platform to unleash the very best of your talents and skills. Together, we’ll celebrate and reward success! Are you intrigued? Then read on and apply now to advance your career at Ledgebrook.

About the Role

We are seeking experienced Cyber Liability underwriting talent to join our growing team whose mission is focused on building a profitable book of cyber liability business. Our vision is to deliver market relevant solutions to our key wholesale trading partners in a more frictionless environment that places an emphasis on efficiencies and quality to meet or exceed our broker’s overall needs in a risk differentiated manner. If you possess an entrepreneurial passion that includes a proven track history of delivering underwriting excellence and are seeking an opportunity to break out of the traditional insurance company mould, we’re looking for you!

As a member of the Cyber team, you will regularly interact with our wholesale trading partners over the phone, virtually and in-person to drive submission flow and convert on the best opportunities quoted. We are looking for disciplined underwriting candidates that possess a strong overall cyber liability background with experience underwriting risks of all industries and sizes.

We are flexible with both a candidate’s experience level and physical work location. The actual position title (Underwriter, Senior UW, AVP, etc.) will be dependent on a candidate’s specific experience and qualifications. We currently operate in a fully remote work environment, so we’re more focused on your experience and cultural fit than where you physically sit!

About You

Here at Ledgebrook we’re passionate about creating a team that thrives on continuous learning and shares our excitement about building a company from the ground up. We’re looking for people to join us with:

● A passion for delivering world-class customer service to our internal and external customers

● Intellectual curiosity and a strong desire for innovation, rather than following the status quo

● A hunger for continuous learning and opportunities to grow

● Agile prioritization skills coupled with a keen sense of urgency - we balance getting it right with getting it done right now

● A strong drive and desire to win together as a high-performing team

● A moral compass to "do the right thing, period." We have zero tolerance for toxic behaviors

● An eagerness to actively participate and connect with the whole team, across remote locations

● An honest, transparent communication style

● A proactive, solution-oriented mindset. We don’t look for blame, we look for the solution

As a future Cyber Liability Underwriter, your experience and qualifications must include:

● 2+ years experience as a cyber underwriter

● Experience working in the Cyber E&S market; Tech E&O experience is a plus

● Ability to work as a team player or independently in a fast-paced work environment

● Deep wholesale broker trading relationships

● Effective communication skills to articulate our appetite and develop wholesale broker relationships

● Understanding of pricing and risk selection criteria to achieve underwriting profit

● Advanced understanding of data analysis and execution of portfolio management objectives

● Intellectual curiosity, problem solving skills, and a sense of urgency

● Responsive, customer service focused mindset and behaviors

● Ability to make timely decisions with appropriate information and consultation

● A strong entrepreneurial drive and desire to build and win together as a high performing team

● Ability to travel to meet with assigned brokers or with the broader team to participate in industry conference or events
